In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lh is a hyperpolarization‐dependent cation current that is present in the dopaminergie neurons and is not involved in the generation of the spontaneous pacemaker discharge.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lh is a voltage‐gated cation current that is activated by hyperpolarization and is carried by a mixture of Na+ and Ca2+.

lh is not a significant factor underlying either the spontaneous pacemaker discharge or the setting of the resting potential level of these cells, but it may be a factor in modulating their excitability by limiting their hyperpolarization.
lh is an important determinant for the membrane properties of the dopaminergically identified midbrain neurons, and may be a target for drugs affecting dopaminergic function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hyperpolarization‐dependent inward cation current, lh, which has been shown to play a major role in the generation of the pacemaker activity of the dopaminigergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, does not contribute significantly to the setting of their normal resting membrane potential.

the hyperpolarization‐induced inward current (lh), which is a typical feature in dopaminergic neurons in the midbrain, is neither a significant contributor to the spontaneous pacemaker discharge nor to the resting membrane potential level of these neurons.

the lh channel in dopaminergic cells is a hyperpolarization‐dependent, slowly activating and noninactivating current that is blocked by caesium and is not significantly affected by TTX, TEA or barium.
